data.text: Cybersickness evaluation strategies can be organized into three aspects: input, process, and output. Interpretable models offer more flexibility and provide precise details about the relationships between the input and the output. Black-box models generally provide higher prediction accuracy than transparent and interpretable models but require large amounts of data and processing power. Hybrid models combine different machine learning models to provide high accuracy and some transparency.
points: Cybersickness evaluation strategies can be organized into three aspects: input, process, and output.
Interpretable models offer more flexibility and provide precise details about the relationships between input and output.
Black-box models generally provide higher prediction accuracy but require large amounts of data and processing power.
Hybrid models combine different machine learning models to provide high accuracy and some transparency.

data.text: Cybersickness evaluation is categorized into detection, which occurs after an experience, and prediction, which occurs before. While most research focuses on detection, prediction is important because it can enable mitigation measures before cybersickness occurs. Evaluation outputs can be classification labels indicating the likelihood of sickness or numerical scores generally produced by regression models to quantify severity.
points: Cybersickness evaluation is categorized into detection (after an experience) and prediction (before an experience).
Most research focuses on detection, but prediction is important for enabling mitigation measures.
Evaluation outputs can be classification labels indicating likelihood or numerical scores quantifying severity.

data.text: Because complete prevention of cybersickness is generally not possible, mitigation measures are used to lessen its impact. These measures involve a trade-off between reducing cybersickness and preserving user experience. Mitigation must also be considered from both the developer's and the user's perspectives.
points: Mitigation measures lessen the impact of cybersickness because complete prevention is generally not possible.
Mitigating cybersickness involves a trade-off between reducing the sickness and preserving user experience.
Mitigation must be considered from both the developer's and the user's perspectives.

data.text: Developers can mitigate cybersickness by using field of view (FOV) adjustment to restrict peripheral optical flow. Other visual strategies include dynamic visual blur, rest frames, and optical-flow manipulation. Hardware-level alterations and modified locomotion techniques also provide various ways to reduce or prevent cybersickness.
points: Field of view (FOV) adjustment can mitigate cybersickness by restricting peripheral optical flow.
Dynamic visual blur, rest frames, and optical-flow manipulation are visual techniques used to reduce cybersickness.
Hardware-level alterations can modify or replace equipment to reduce or eliminate cybersickness.
Locomotion techniques can be modified or proposed as new methods to prevent cybersickness.

data.text: Users need personal countermeasures because cybersickness is subjective and individual. To reduce risk, users should limit exposure to a safe maximum of 55 to 70 minutes or use habituation through repeated short-duration exposures. Additionally, techniques like controlled breathing, background music, and airflow can help soothe the mind and reduce symptoms.
points: Users need personal countermeasures because cybersickness is subjective and individual.
Users should avoid long exposure, as a safe maximum for many is between 55 and 70 minutes.
Habituation can be achieved through repeated short-duration exposures.
Controlled breathing, background music, and airflow can help soothe the mind and reduce symptoms.
